title: Michigan's 4th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Michigan's 4th Congressional District will determine who represents this south-central Michigan district in the U.S. House. The district includes parts of Ingham, Livingston, and Oakland counties, and has been represented by Republican Bill Huizenga since 2023 after redistricting. The race is expected to be competitive, with both parties fielding candidates in a district that has shifted politically in recent cycles. Key issues include the economy, healthcare, and local infrastructure.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of the research date.

candidates.name: Bill Huizenga
candidates.summary: Bill Huizenga is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2010. He serves on the House Financial Services Committee and is known for his conservative fiscal policies and support for small businesses. Huizenga previously served in the Michigan House of Representatives.

career_history.title: U.S. Representative
career_history.description: Representing Michigan's 2nd and later 4th Congressional Districts

candidates.name: Jessica Swartz
candidates.summary: Jessica Swartz is a Democratic candidate running for Michigan's 4th Congressional District in 2026. She is a small business owner and community advocate focused on healthcare access and economic opportunity. Swartz has not held elected office previously.

forecast.rationale: No public polling is available for this race, so this informational forecast relies on non-polling factors in the provided race data. Bill Huizenga benefits from incumbency and long congressional experience, which gives Republicans a modest structural edge. However, the district is described as competitive and politically shifting, and the Democratic challenger is a credible major-party nominee, which limits the strength of any Republican advantage. With sparse evidence and no polling to validate the race environment, the contest is best characterized as narrowly favoring Republicans.
